extract: The consolidated net loss of IndiGo narrowed 27.2 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to ₹1,879.1 crore in the September quarter of FY27, with stronger revenues and pricing aiding in cushioning the impact of a 67.2 per cent surge in fuel expenses.

During the post-results conference call with analysts, IndiGo Chief Executive Officer Willie Walsh said the near-term outlook remained challenging, with costs elevated despite stronger revenue performance.

Chief Financial Officer Kiran Thadimarri said the Singapore Jet Fuel Index was 60 per cent higher than a year earlier, while rupee depreciation further increased the cost of fuel and other dollar-denominated expenses (such as aircraft-leasing charges).The airline will end

InterGlobe Aviation Ltd, the parent company of IndiGo, on Thursday reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 1,879 crore for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27), narrowing 27.2 percent from a loss of Rs 2,582 crore in the corresponding

The country's largest airline by market share reported a 25.9 percent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 23,364 crore, compared with Rs 18,555 crore a year earlier, supported by higher passenger yields and disciplined capacity deployment.

However, IndiGo's net loss excluding foreign exchange effects stood at Rs 723.7 crore, compared with a profit of Rs 103.9 crore in the year-ago quarter, indicating deterioration in underlying profitability despite the narrower reported loss.
